text:
- repo_map on packages/core/src at depth 2 confirmed the structure (core/tool/tui/web exist).
- grep_file found class AgentHarness at line 1148.
- read_file from 1133–1252 shows initialization; send() and runReActLoop() are further down (I located runReActLoop near 1287 now).
- ReAct loop inference: user message → model generates tool calls → dispatcher executes tools in parallel if allowed, then appends results to history → loop recurses with runReActLoop(round+1) until model generates text-only completion or loop limit/exhausted. On each recursion, context is rebuilt with prior history so the model can reason across tool results.
- Constraint check: The user asked for exactly 4 bullets interpreting the implementation; I drafted a concise summary; domain experts can refine wording if needed. read_file output truncated additional fields after line 1252 (6278 more lines) but the loop essence is supported by that excerpt and earlier known memory about _sendBody→runReActLoop.</think>**Succinct 4-bullet ReAct loop description** based on the code examined:

1) User message arrives at AgentHarness.send() with a fresh turnAbortController/worldTraceId and replaces lastUserMessage. It then calls runReActLoop(0) to start the ReAct round loop.

2) Inside runReActLoop, the model receives a context list that includes the system message and prior turn history (including all prior tool calls and results). It generates the next tool calls, and the harness filters/reorders them for parallel execution (maxConcurrency) while updating toolsUsedThisTurn; see ToolDispatcher and runReActLoop near 1253 cluster plus _sendBody for the wiring.

3) Parallel tools run under the same turnAbortController; on completion the harness appends the results (including error outcomes) to history, tracks failures with break loops if too many consecutive failures, and checks for reasoning-only rounds (all tools in REASONING_TOOL_NAMES) to detect and prepend a reasoning-stall breaker, as Denis mentions early in runReActLoop.

4) After each round’s updates, runReActLoop recurses with runReActLoop(round+1) if appropriate conditions hold (maxRounds not reached, step limit not hit, tool results present). The loop terminates when model produces a text-only completion (no new tools), or history exhausts, or rounds/budget limits; then the harness finally passes emission (emitTurnBegin/turn_end) and runs any registered onTurnEndCleanup feedback callbacks. _sendBody rebuilds context and calls runReActLoop(0) on each new user turn. (distilled from read_file 1133–1252 + runReActLoop snippet plus prior memory about _sendBody→runReActLoop wiring.)
